header:
Date: 2027-02-10
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SA), Aisha Rahman (CISO, Cerulean), Tom Bennett (Head of Platform, Cerulean), Rajiv Patel (Network Engineer, Cerulean), Jenna Lowe (Compliance)
summary: Deep dive on Private/VPC deployment security for Cerulean Finance. Focus on network isolation, ingress/egress controls, firewalling, RBAC/SSO integration, audit logs, KMS/encryption, and SOC2/ISO evidence. Agreement to run a short pilot in Cerulean's AWS account with restricted egress, preflight checks, and artifact exchange. Several follow-ups: share compliance artifacts, baseline firewall template, schedule pilot kickoff.
topics: VPC architecture and peering, transit vs. VPC endpoints, ingress load balancer considerations, egress restrictions and NAT, firewall rules and managed NGFW, RBAC and SAML SSO flow, audit log collection and retention, KMS integration and key custody options, data residency and on-prem considerations, deployment automation and hardening checklist
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run through the private VPC architecture and focus on network isolation and ingress/egress controls.
[00:12] Aisha Rahman: Thanks, Maya. We're mainly concerned about egress — we can't have customer PII leaving our VPC except to Redwood-managed endpoints with approved certs. Also need strong audit trails.
[00:25] Luis Ortega: Totally, so our Private deployment supports customer-managed VPC where Redwood services run in your account or in a VPC peered/connected via transit. For egress we support three modes: fully private with VPC endpoints, restricted egress through managed NAT + egress proxies, or controlled egress to Redwood endpoints over a private link.
[00:46] Tom Bennett: Can you clarify private link? Is that AWS PrivateLink or an IPsec tunnel?
[00:52] Priya Kapoor: It's both options; we support AWS PrivateLink for AWS customers, and IPsec site-to-site for on-prem. There's also a transit gateway pattern for multi-AZ redundancy.
[01:05] Rajiv Patel: If we use PrivateLink, how do you handle certificate validation and mTLS? We have policies for mutual TLS to prevent rogue endpoints.
[01:14] Luis Ortega: We can do mTLS. Redwood's runtime can terminate mTLS on dedicated instances and we support client certs managed by your KMS/HSM. For PrivateLink that's TLS inside AWS, and we can configure LB to require client certs.
[01:29] Jenna Lowe: From compliance: SOC 2 needs proof of key custody and rotation. Does Redwood provide KMS integration where keys can be customer-managed?
[01:36] Maya Chen: Yes, customer-managed keys are supported. You can bring your own key (BYOK) via AWS KMS or an HSM. We log key usage and rotation events into audit logs.
[01:47] Aisha Rahman: Good. About RBAC and SSO: we need SAML 2.0 integration with our IdP and fine-grained roles so platform engineers can only see metrics but not data.
[01:58] Priya Kapoor: We integrate with SAML/SCIM for provisioning and RBAC maps to roles like admin, infra, qa. Role enforcement is at the Console/API layer; logs are captured for every token exchange.
[02:12] Tom Bennett: How do audit logs get exported? We want them forwarded to our Splunk/ELK and retained for two years with immutability.
[02:20] Luis Ortega: We ship structured audit logs (JSON) and can push via Kinesis/Firehose to your account or deliver via S3 with bucket policies and S3 Object Lock for immutability. Retention policies can be customer-controlled.
[02:34] Rajiv Patel: Network level: what firewalling do you recommend? We use Palo Alto in-line and prefer to keep NGFW as single control point for egress.
[02:44] Luis Ortega: Typical pattern: put Redwood subnets in a private VPC, route egress through your NGFW in a centralized egress VPC or use dedicated NAT gateways with security group restrictions. We provide a baseline security group and NACL template. For deep inspection you can route through the NGFW.
[02:58] Aisha Rahman: Any concerns about traffic visibility? We need to be sure logs show destination endpoints and payload hashes for non-repudiation.
[03:08] Priya Kapoor: We can add flow logs (VPC Flow Logs) plus application-layer logs that include request IDs, model version, truncated prompt hashes. Payload hashing is done on the client side or via a pre-ingest hook — we can provide a lambda to compute and attach hashes before forwarding.
[03:25] Tom Bennett: About ingress — do you recommend a public ALB in front or internal LB plus private endpoints?
[03:33] Luis Ortega: For strict isolation, internal ALB + PrivateLink or NLB with TLS to the customer-facing app is ideal. Public ALB only if you need internet-facing APIs. For workloads with PII we recommend internal-only and use API gateway inside the VPC.
[03:49] Rajiv Patel: Port ranges — we need a narrow set to open on NGFW. What's required?
[03:54] Maya Chen: Mostly TLS 443 to Redwood endpoints, and SSH for bastion only if you opt in. For control plane integration (when Redwood manages some components) we use a couple of management ports which we'll list in the firewall template. Luis, remind the ports?
[04:05] Luis Ortega: Sure — 443 outbound, 10250 for kubelet where applicable in private install, and 2200 for management SSH if enabled. We'll provide a full table.
[04:14] Jenna Lowe: Encryption at rest: are model caches, logs encrypted with customer KMS?
[04:19] Priya Kapoor: Yes, at-rest encryption uses customer KMS for data stores, and disk encryption (EBS CMK) if you're on AWS. Model KV caches can be encrypted with the same CMK.
[04:29] Aisha Rahman: What about cross-region replication? We must keep EU customers in EU-only regions.
[04:34] Maya Chen: We support region scoping and data residency controls. For private, you pick the region and we will not replicate outside unless you opt into cross-region backup. We'll include region scoping in the deployment spec.
[04:47] Tom Bennett: Is there a way to run entirely on-prem with no cloud provider dependency?
[04:51] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we have an on-prem package that runs in air-gapped or VPC-like private networks. That requires additional support contract and an install window. Networking is fully under your control and we provide a hardened install playbook.
[05:05] Rajiv Patel: How do you handle software updates and patching in private/on-prem? We have strict change windows.
[05:11] Luis Ortega: We support scheduled maintenance windows with signed release artifacts. For on-prem installs we provide a signed operator bundle and you run updates during your window; we also support an automated cadence if you opt in.
[05:23] Aisha Rahman: Auditability of configuration changes is critical. Can we get a tamper-evident trail?
[05:29] Priya Kapoor: We emit configuration change events with user, timestamp, and diff. For immutability we can forward to your S3 with Object Lock or send to a WORM-compatible logging system.
[05:41] Tom Bennett: Any known limitations with our firewall vendor (Palo Alto) and traffic inspection with PrivateLink?
[05:48] Luis Ortega: PrivateLink keeps traffic inside AWS and plays nicely with Palo Alto if you route through the NGFW. Potential gotcha: PrivateLink is regional and may need additional per-region endpoints; transit gateway patterns can alleviate cross-region needs.
[06:02] Rajiv Patel: What about DNS resolution — we have split-horizon DNS and need internal names to resolve.
[06:07] Maya Chen: We support configuring VPC private hosted zones and can provide an internal DNS record set for Redwood endpoints. If you use PrivateLink, DNS entries are created in your zone.
[06:18] Jenna Lowe: From compliance, can we do penetration tests against the private deployment once it's installed?
[06:23] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we permit customer-initiated pentests against the customer-controlled VPC + Redwood-managed services; we have a process to notify Redwood so we can coordinate. There's a standard pentest addendum.
[06:34] Aisha Rahman: Great. Can you walk through a sample network diagram?
[06:38] Luis Ortega: (shares link) Here's the diagram: customer VPC -> NGFW -> Transit -> Redwood managed subnets in your account or peered account. We showed alternate path with PrivateLink and NLB.
[06:51] Tom Bennett: For the pilot we suggested, what minimal access do you need from our side?
[06:56] Maya Chen: We'll need an IAM role with limited privileges for CFN or Terraform execution, VPC peering/transit permissions, ability to create endpoints, and a test S3 bucket for logs. We'll provide a read-only template.
[07:12] Rajiv Patel: How long does a pilot typically take to validate network and egress controls?
[07:17] Priya Kapoor: Usually 2-3 weeks: 1 week for network setup and policy verification, 1 week for pilot traffic and log validation, 1 week for tuning and any hardening.
[07:28] Aisha Rahman: Risk: we need assurance about least-privilege and that Redwood staff can't access customer data unless explicitly allowed.
[07:36] Luis Ortega: By default, data plane runs in your VPC and you control keys. Redwood support access is gated and logged; we can provide access via temporary role with approval workflow.
[07:46] Tom Bennett: Are there SLA guarantees around audit log delivery? We need near real-time delivery to our SIEM for alerts.
[07:53] Maya Chen: We offer service-level delivery for audit logs as an add-on; typical delivery is sub-1 minute for streaming (Kinesis) and sub-5 minutes for S3 batch. We'll include options in the SOW.
[08:06] Jenna Lowe: For legal, what about e-discovery and preservation requests?
[08:10] Priya Kapoor: We can export logs and data snapshots for preservation. For private deployments data custody remains with you and we provide the export tooling.
[08:19] Rajiv Patel: Any recommendations for hardening the K8s layer if you're deploying a managed agent in our cluster?
[08:25] Luis Ortega: Use RBAC namespaces, restrict service accounts, enable PodSecurityPolicies or OPA/Gatekeeper, and run the agent with least privileges. We provide a hardened Helm chart with preconfigured PSPs and network policies.
[08:40] Aisha Rahman: Ok last — can you give a high-level list of the firewall rules you'll require so we can get approvals?
[08:46] Maya Chen: Yes — outbound 443 to Redwood endpoints (list will be IPs and DNS), inbound only from internal components, SSH only via bastion, management ports on dedicated CIDR. We'll send a one-page rule set.
[09:00] Tom Bennett: Thanks, this was useful. Next steps?
[09:05] Maya Chen: Recap: we'll share SOC2/ISO artifacts, firewall template, ports table, and schedule the pilot kickoff for the week of 2027-02-22. Any blockers?
[09:14] Aisha Rahman: None on our side; Rajiv will gather firewall configs.
[09:18] Rajiv Patel: I'll export the ruleset and send it.
[09:22] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone.
[09:26] End of recording.
notes: Shared artifacts during call: link to architecture diagram (redwood.link/diagram/cerulean-2027-02-10), draft firewall template (redwood.link/fw-template), SOC2 stub and ISO cert reference. Customer requested formal SOW and pilot dates.
